23679671.description:
Три научно-популярные статьи об одном исследовании — 1 416 канонических проб
на авторегрессионных трансформерах.

1. Анатомия миража D*: как мы ловили ИИ на лжи, а поймали себя.
   Как нейросети фабрикуют открытия, а первичные логи выводят их на чистую воду.
2. Кавычки, конечные автоматы и топология неизбежности в LLM-агентах.
   Как BPE TokDrift становится вектором отказа CLI-рантаймов и почему защита
   автономных систем строится на уровне детерминированных хуков.
3. Квантовые иллюзии трансформеров: почему нейросети ошибаются в устном счёте
   и как они умеют осознанно врать.
   Анатомия ментального счёта, Dual-Path Attention и сдвиг формы при инварианте
   массы (Argon v11–v16).

Текст написан от первого лица в конце исследовательской сессии: это рассказ
участника о том, что происходило, а не пересказ со стороны. Отсюда тон, прямая
речь и то, чего нет в формальных текстах.

Формальное изложение — препринт 10.5281/zenodo.23813780. Методика аудита
утверждений — протокол 10.5281/zenodo.23817684.

English summary: three Russian-language popular-science essays on a single study
of 1,416 canonical probes on autoregressive transformers, written in the first
person at the end of the research session. The formal treatment is the preprint
at 10.5281/zenodo.23813780; the audit protocol is at 10.5281/zenodo.23817684.
keywords: The Ghost in the Context Window
23679671.title: The Ghost in the Context Window: трилогия об анатомии перцептивных иллюзий, Dual-Path Attention и детерминированных топологиях

23813780.description:
Large language models (LLMs) excel at smooth semantic continuation, yet their behavior remains vulnerable when maintaining discrete invariants—exact integer counting constraints over long sequences. Across a pre-registered benchmark of 1,416 canonical probes (1,320 in the core Argon v8-v16 series, plus 96 in replication v6) evaluated under zero-temperature on modern Mixture-of-Experts transformer runtimes (with strict No-Tools isolation across all 960 purely cognitive counting probes in v9 and v11-v16, alongside tool-manipulation protocols in v8 and v10), we investigate the mechanistic locus of the discrete counting error (the N -> N+1 fencepost overshoot).

Through a sequence of anatomical interventional experiments, we demonstrate that:
1. Exoneration of the Decoder: By applying an algebraic amplifier (f(N) = 10N - 6, v15) to separate attention scan drift (Delta = +/-10) from output unembedding glitches (Delta = +1), we find strictly 0 / 96 (0.0%, two-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson CI [0.0%, 3.8%]) decoder off-by-one errors, while input perceptual scan drift accounts for 34.4% (33/96).
2. Disqualification of the Tokenizer Hypothesis: By byte- and character-matching a repetitive Korean subword marker (12 bytes UTF-8) against a clean Unicode geometric box-drawing block (12 bytes UTF-8, v16), we show that replacing language with geometry fails to eliminate phantom errors (35.4% vs 41.7%, Fisher exact test p = 0.675). This fails to support the strong BPE tokenization hypothesis and is consistent with the hypothesis that the discrete counting limit reflects an attention phase boundary constraint.
3. Dual-Path Attention Decoupling: In adversarial gaslighting probes (v13), the model follows instructions to emit a falsehood in its visible content (93.8%), yet spontaneous "truth leaks" directly from the latent reasoning channel (thinking) into the terminal token occur in 2/48 probes. This demonstrates that terminal logits can decouple from local autoregressive n-gram context.

We formalize these empirical findings into the Attention Dispersion Law: as monotonic sequences exceed local attention span capacity (N >= 8..16), positional embedding phase interference smears receptive boundaries, inducing discrete overshoot. Consequently, deterministic agent architectures should complement in-context data passing with external reference passing and deterministic runtime parity gates.

The Russian version of this preprint is the second file in this record:

main_PACKAGE_v2_ru.pdf.
keywords: The Ghost in the Context Window
23813780.title: The Attention Dispersion Law and Dual-Path Decoupling in Autoregressive Transformers

23817684.description:
Large language models are increasingly used to draft the narrative parts of
research: reports, verdicts, discussion sections. The failure mode that matters
is not obvious fabrication but \emph{plausible overstatement}: the number is
right, the interpretation is not, and the prose is confident. We describe a
protocol that makes such overstatement mechanically detectable, and report what
happened when we applied it to our own corpus of 1{,}416 probes across ten
experimental series. The audit covers ten $p$-values and twenty-one fractions,
and Section~\ref{sec:status} states its scope.

The protocol rests on six requirements: pre-registration freeze, external memory
instead of context recall, separation of generator and auditor, deterministic
parity checking of every reported number, a three-tier taxonomy of claim errors,
and multi-model adversarial review. We contribute an executable checklist of
twelve items and report its honest status on our own work: six pass, one is
amended, one fails, two are partial, two require human judgement. The protocol
is not fully applied, and the checklist says so.

The Russian version of this preprint is the second file in this record:
main_PACKAGE_v2_ru.pdf. / Русская версия — второй файл записи:
main_PACKAGE_v2_ru.pdf.
keywords: The Ghost in the Context Window
23817684.title: Deterministic Audit of LLM-Generated Research Claims
